section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces the psychological benefits of gratitude and highlights the need to investigate moderators. The authors propose ambivalence over emotional expression as a potential moderator. Two studies were conducted: Study 1 involved 353 Taiwanese college students, and Study 2 involved 233 Taiwanese college students. Both studies examined the moderating effect of ambivalence over emotional expression on the relationship between gratitude and well-being, including happiness, loneliness, and depression.
